- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong upward bias in high-volatility periods (e.g., 2023-02), particularly when true prices show sharp declines after peaks.
- Forecasts often fail to capture mean reversion in the short term (1–3 days) after a peak, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true prices show sudden drops or corrections.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term volatility, leading to underestimation of sharp downward moves in the last 5–10 days.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 5–15% in the final 5–10 days if the prior 5–10 days show a clear downward trend or volatility spike.
- Model overestimates prices when the 30-day history shows a recent upward trend — should reduce forecast by 3–8% for such cases.
- Model underestimates prices when the 30-day history shows a recent downward trend — should increase forecast by 3–8% for such cases.
- Model fails to adjust for lagged price corrections — should add a 1–3 day lag correction for downward moves in the true outcome.
